stem: Chirag must divide the $12$ cm by $9$ cm rectangle in the diagram into identical squares that fill it with no gaps and no overlaps.

parts.text: Which claim correctly plans the equal segments?

options.text: Mark equal $3$ cm segments along the $12$ cm and $9$ cm sides so squares of side $3$ cm fill the rectangle.
Mark segments of length $12$ cm only, and ignore making the $9$ cm side match equal square sides.
The rough diagram of the rectangle produces identical squares even when corresponding sides are unequal.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Identical squares need equal side lengths; 3 cm divides both 12 cm and 9 cm, so equal 3 cm segments tile the rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Side length must divide both 12 and 9; 3 cm works and forces equal segments on both sides. Using only the 12 cm length omits the identical-square equal-side condition. Claiming the rough diagram alone produces identical squares reverses the equal-segment plan.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source grid quadrilateral as a 12 cm by 9 cm rectangle with dashed 3 cm tiling lines.
